title: Animated ‘Zootopia’ Breaks Disney Record
main_content:
Last weekend, the latest Disney movie, “Zootopia,” broke records.

The movie had the largest opening weekend for a Disney animated film. People across the United States bought more than $75 million worth of tickets.

Already, the movie’s worldwide box office total is more than $230 million.

“Zootopia” is a city of animals. The movie stars a bunny rabbit police officer and a fox criminal who team up to find a missing otter.

Critics have strongly praised “Zootopia” for its sharp humor and strong message. The film explores racism and other intolerance.

Jared Bush and Phil Johnston wrote “Zootopia.” They told reporters that it started out as a spy movie set in several different animal worlds. But they found the mammal world especially interesting. So they changed the story.

Bush and Johnston said building the imaginary world took a lot of research.

The writers spoke with people who study culture and group behavior. And they talked with animal experts like zookeepers.

questions.question: What topics does the film explore?
options: The relationship between different species of animals
The importance of teamwork in law enforcement

questions.question: Why did the writers of “Zootopia” change the story later on?
options: To focus on a more heroic narrative
They found the mammal world especially interesting
To make the plot more complex
questions.answer: They found the mammal world especially interesting
